Timing.summary: Lap timing, race management and custom race displays for your analogue slotcar track.
Timing.short: Run your races, count every lap and build your race display.
features: Run the whole race night
Practice, qualifying, heats, championships and team endurance—with optional fuel, tyres, weather and pit strategy.
Build your own race screens
Create layouts, widgets, leaderboards and charts for your desk, second display or club TV.
Share your race-day creations
Send another racer your layouts, widgets, audio and image sets, or bundle designs into a Content Pack.

Paddock.summary: A home for your slotcar collection, photographs, parts, setups and maintenance.
Paddock.short: Keep your cars, parts and workshop history together.
features: Your collection, in view
Browse your cars and photographs in a dedicated showroom.
A workshop for every car
Organise parts, setups and maintenance work.
Share a car’s story
Send selected cars with photographs and optional setups. Another collector can review and add them to Paddock.

Circuit.summary: Design it. Build it. Race it. Plan your next circuit before building it for real.
Circuit.short: Design your track, plan your space and export your layout.
features: Design your circuit
Arrange branded track pieces or create routed and FreeForm layouts.
Plan the build
Check your space, compare lane lengths and count the pieces you need.
Pass the layout around
Export an editable track or a reusable piece pack, then let another Circuit user build on your idea.

Telemetry.summary: Explore gearing, motors, tyres and weight, compare setups and analyse recorded lap times.
Telemetry.short: Explore your setup and understand your lap performance.
features: Explore your setup
Work through gearing, motor, tyre and weight calculations.
Read the laps
Compare recorded runs and follow changes in pace and consistency alongside the captured setups.
Share what you discovered
Export a comparison report that friends can read in their browser, with statistics, observations and setup differences.

Livery.summary: Plan paint schemes, stripes, race numbers and decals on editable 2D car templates.
Livery.short: Create the look of your next build with editable car templates.
features: Start with a template
Work on editable 2D car templates.
Make it your own
Explore colours, stripes, race numbers and decals.
Give your design a next chapter
Share templates, liveries or a complete editable project. A friend imports a copy and takes it in a new direction.

Decals.summary: Size and arrange your artwork into decal sheets, then export a PDF for printing.
Decals.short: Turn your artwork into carefully arranged printable decal sheets.
features: Bring your artwork
Organise artwork for your slotcar projects.
From sheet to model
Size and arrange your artwork, check a sizing proof and export a PDF ready for printing at actual size.
Make it. Share it.
Exchange editable sheets and saved decal packs so another builder can resize, rearrange and make them their own.

Paddock: Put your favourite cars, cover photographs and real racing history on display, with a fixed favourite or an automatically changing selection.
Create ordered groups and run a presentation with selected labels, shuffled cars, photographs or racing history.
Keep manufacturer, model, scale, race number and class alongside condition, location, packaging, ownership and valuation.
Build a gallery for each car, attach documents and choose photograph focal points while keeping the originals.
Keep future purchases separate, then move a car into your collection with its information, photographs and history intact.
Compare car specifications, gearing and custom fields, with optional recorded configurations to put measured pace in context.
Browse photographs or a detailed table, then search, filter and sort your collection to find the cars you need.
Add text, choice, number, date, checkbox or notes fields. Choose columns and save useful views for later.
Reuse manufacturers, classes and other library entries, and merge duplicate values to keep your collection consistent.
Record the full-size car’s team, drivers, event, year and results, with sources and reference photographs separate from your model photos.
Export an exact-product template for your own AI, then review sourced factory specifications before importing them. Your modifications stay separate.
Export car cards, setup sheets, scrutineering and inventory reports as PDFs, with purchase information included only when you choose.
Keep owned parts separate from catalogue references, with quantities, individual items, specifications, compatibility and photographs.
Track storage locations and whether parts are available, fitted to a car or held in an assembly.
Collect stock parts and free-text purchases, change quantities, move items between lists and optionally add completed purchases to stock.
Keep purchase orders, receipts, corrections and supplier history, with estimates tracked in their own currencies.
Combine researched catalogue files into one review, resolve duplicates and add references without increasing your owned stock.
Review researched image suggestions before replacing selected pictures, and keep manufacturer or supplier links close to parts and shopping lists.
Choose stock or catalogue components on an exploded car diagram, including bodywork, electronics, magnets and ballast.
Save unfinished plans without consuming stock, review what is missing and send requirements to a shopping list.
Build reusable component groups, then install, remove, transfer or replace them while keeping their history.
Reuse suitable parts, return unused parts to stock and link a rebuilt car to its archived predecessor.
Save factory and current setups, inspect differences and review substitutions or stock transfers before applying changes.
Explore ratio, axle RPM, rollout and theoretical speed, with supported torque, driving-force and ideal motor-power calculations.
Plan maintenance, upgrades, rebuilds, chassis, tyre, motor or bodywork jobs with priorities and due dates.
Break work into steps, add instructions and before/after photographs, then pause, resume, complete or cancel the job.
Link required purchases to the shopping list so unfinished jobs retain the parts they still need.
Record work already carried out and set the next service date to create an upcoming maintenance reminder.
Organise tools, oils, adhesives and consumables with locations, remaining quantities and low-stock information.
Keep PDFs, exploded views and reference images in a searchable workshop library or attach them to a particular car.
Record test results with the track, lane, driver, voltage, direction and magnet conditions, plus the car configuration used.
Receive finalised Timing results with the race-time configuration, including supported corrections and withdrawn results.
Compare average or median pace, consistency and the best five- or ten-lap runs alongside setup differences and test conditions.
Review measured lap history and lane records while keeping manually entered tests separate from recorded timing results.
Make supported car configurations available to Timing, and let Telemetry read recorded results for further analysis.
Use the supported same-computer Paddock and Timing library workflow under one operating-system account, with car information and history retained.
Share cars and keep your collection safe
Export selected cars with their main photograph and optional extra photos or setups. Private purchase details and workshop information stay out of public car exports.
Import shared car files and choose which information to accept, including the supported Timing car format.
Scan a QR code on a phone or tablet on the same network to add a car or upload photographs to an existing one.
Share an official collection between trusted home or club computers, with review for important changes while the host stays running.
Choose the fields, photographs, setups and history to retain, and keep retired records archived rather than silently losing their past.
Back up and restore the complete collection for recovery or moving computers, including private data that is excluded from shared car files.
Circuit: Build with the pieces you own
Browse Carrera, Scalextric, Policar, ScaleAuto, Ninco, SCX, AFX, Carrera GO!!!, Carrera Hybrid and Fleischmann packs. Exact and reference-only coverage varies by piece.
Snap track ends together, align parallel straights and nest matching curves for layouts with more than two lanes.
Rotate, mirror, duplicate and select multiple pieces, with Undo/Redo while you try different layouts.
Add matching borders and adjust the drawing order where roads cross or overlap.
Give straight lengths and curve radii distinct catalogue and canvas colours, then return to the normal track artwork whenever you like.
Define straights, curves, borders and lane changers with your own road width, slot spacing, lane count and connector family.
Create nested R1, R2, R3 and larger curves, with a preview of how the road radii and lane spacing fit together.
Measure, check and finish the layout
Check open ends, piece counts, the footprint including borders and nominal lane lengths where the geometry supports them.
Measure the plan or trace a calibrated reference image. Save measurements with the design and include selected dimensions in its PDF report.
Compare required pieces with the quantities you own, then export a shopping CSV for what is missing.
Search combinations of up to four catalogue pieces, preview a possible connection and add it to the layout.
Move grouped pieces together, lock finished sections and preview compatible replacements anchored at either end.
Colour tight slot radii and inspect approximate car-overhang envelopes using car dimensions and an optional drift allowance.
Adjust spacing smoothly inside supported straights or corners while retaining normal end connections, then save a reusable custom variant.
Design individual wooden pieces with their own outlines, or route a continuous layout within the table boundary.
Set lane spacing, slot width and depth, board thickness, edge clearances and braid or tape dimensions.
Combine straight sections, circular corners and Bézier bends with draggable handles, direction locks and exact coordinates.
Preview Fill closing gap, Bridge selected ends or Reshape to close, then adjust the connection or undo it.
Bring lanes together or move them apart through a bend or straight, with smooth transitions back to normal spacing.
Inspect slot or conductor folds, overlaps and tight radii, with estimated slot and conductor lengths for supported geometry.
Draw one lane, generate the others
Shape a continuous slot with Bézier curves, choose which lane it represents and generate the surrounding lanes at your chosen spacing.
Insert points without changing the curve, move several anchors together, lock finished points and adjust curve handles.
Squeeze or spread lanes across several curves, choosing where the change peaks and how gradually it returns to normal.
Distribute ramp heights across a stretch or set point heights and headroom for an upper passage.
Preview smoother joins with anchors held in place, or convert a supported routed-section layout into an editable FreeForm approximation.
Save unfinished drawings, send completed designs to the builder and return to their editable points from the Track Library.
Plan around a rectangular or L-shaped table, with cut-outs, dimensions and a locked position while arranging the circuit.
Arrange boards with dimensions, snapping, duplication, 90-degree rotation and locks, then inspect the combined surface and gaps.
Preview horizontal or vertical board splits and review seams against stock-sheet or transport constraints.
Arrange panels with margins, gaps and optional 90-degree rotation to estimate the sheets needed for a supported flat routed design.
Inspect deck thickness, bridge clearance and joined endpoint heights as part of the track plan.
Export numbered panel outlines and trimmed slots or braids in SVG/DXF packages, with an assembly PDF showing panel positions.
Watch two cars follow supported closed circuits, with illustrative acceleration, braking, cornering and drift settings.
Choose a car-size preset or enter dimensions, then save a motion profile for the design.
Export supported lane routes, artwork, timing-line information and tuning for Timing’s Live Track display.
Exchange track or custom-pack JSON files so another user can open a design or add your reusable pieces.
Export a layout report, a picture with optional transparency, or a CSV parts list for planning the physical build.
Export supported construction paths, including full-size millimetre DXF and SVG scale options, for further work in CAD/CAM.
Save named circuits, search your designs and reopen tracks or reusable custom packs for the next project.
Try Circuit online with storage in your browser, or use the desktop app, which saves on your computer.
Export a workspace backup to move designs between computers or browser workspaces and protect them before clearing local data.
Timing: Get familiar with the track, set a benchmark and prepare the grid before the race.
Choose the finish rule, start-light sequence and first-lap behaviour for your event.
Create reusable rotation plans, move drivers or teams through lanes and combine the results.
Link rounds with rosters, points tables, bonuses, dropped results, teams and tie-breaks.
Run teams with swap windows, minimum driving requirements, stint records and swap penalties.
Keep overall and class classifications, or give each lane a timed-use allowance with expiry warnings.
Set tank sizes, consumption, refuelling speeds and the consequences of an empty tank.
Choose compounds, lifespan, weather suitability, available sets, warnings and mandatory stops.
Simulate cold, working and hot tyres with compound-specific heating, cooling and wear effects.
Plan changing conditions, tyre suitability, wrong-tyre penalties and supported race effects.
Make faster laps consume more fuel or tyres, and slower laps conserve them using your chosen pace rules.
Configure supported damage events, their effects and the repairs or retirement required by your rules.
Create points tiers, named penalties, time additions, lap adjustments, forced stops and disqualification rules.
Set target pace, speeding penalties, pit-time changes and optional random flags with conditions.
Balance cars through fuel consumption, refuelling speed and optional tank capacity. Requires a Fuel System.
Limit tyre sets, repair credits and replacement supplies across a race, event or championship.
Combine fuel, tyre and repair work sequentially or in parallel, with timed or manual release.
Manage track calls and red-flag restarts, then review laps, disqualifications and the classification before saving.
Move, resize and layer widgets in separate layouts for the main screen and a second display.
Create reusable displays from values, labels, images, gauges, bars and conditional indicators.
Bring essential driver, timing or race information together without arranging every value separately.
Choose values, row widths, labels, colours and overall or supported class views for live and finished races.
Design lap trends, driver comparisons, delta trends, box plots, histograms, position histories and heatmaps.
Use state colours, lap flashes, record highlights, lane accents and horizontal, vertical or segmented resource bars.
Build messages with supported driver names, lap times, positions, gaps and Race System status.
Combine recordings, effects and ambience with playback conditions, repeat limits and voice/mix options.
Use your own avatars, lights, tyres and weather artwork, then add a logo, header images and colours.
Celebrate results with podium cards, driver facts, comparison charts or a saved leaderboard design.
Keep records linked to drivers, cars and tracks. Red-flag-interrupted laps are excluded from records.
Review laps, distance, sessions, wins, fastest laps, last use and mileage or laps since servicing.
Show live timing on a monitor or TV, or let devices on the same local network follow along in a browser.
Use password-protected director access for supported race controls, warnings and recent-event information.
Import supported Circuit lane routes and artwork. Car movement is estimated from lap timing, not continuous position sensing.
Connect to a Paddock Dealership, race cached car configurations and queue finalised results for delivery back.
Use supported Trackmate or Arduino interfaces and documented alternatives. DS-200/300 and Windows Parallel Port support have hardware-verification limits; see the guide.
Replay saved lap sequences as opponents, or explore with keyboard/manual controls and simulated inputs.
Export individual creations and related items. Other users import copies without exchanging their entire database.
Bundle supported screens, widgets, charts, leaderboards, image/audio sets, themes and Race System presets without writing code.
Export drivers, cars, tracks, teams, Race Systems, championships, leaderboard/chart designs and saved sessions.
Move or recover an installation with its database, artwork, sounds, settings and race history. Restoring replaces the current database.
Extend Timing with separately installed drivers, widgets, pages, tools and race rules. Run plugins only from authors you trust.
Explore grouped help, setup explanations, previews and worked examples of the rules behind the racing.
Telemetry: Start with how the car feels
Guided Driver Feedback
Work through handling symptoms such as sliding, tipping, hopping or inconsistent braking, with optional measurements and targeted follow-up questions.
Suggested checks and tests
Explore possible causes, ballast, gearing or magnetic options, with trade-offs and a practical test to try next.
Record what helped
Mark checks as looking OK, a problem or uncertain, then record whether a test improved, preserved or worsened the behaviour of that setup.
Chassis geometry
Measure the guide-to-rear-axle triangle and inspect a scale drawing, angles and geometry ratios.
Guided weighing
Use supported axle, guide-and-rear or individual-rear-wheel weighing methods, with repeated readings and total-mass checks.
Static balance and ballast
Explore load distribution and centre of gravity, then plan added, removed or moved ballast separately from your measured setup.
Gearing, tyres and motor performance
Live workbench
Enter the measurements you have and see gear ratio, axle RPM, rollout, theoretical speed and supported torque or power results update.
Motor torque and power curves
Explore ideal brushed-DC curves and move a shared operating-point slider when matching-voltage motor ratings and stall torque are available.
Gear finder
Search pinion and driven-gear ranges for rollout targets or tyre-size compensation, with candidate combinations to check for physical fit.
Tyre preparation and life
Explore diameter, clearance, left/right wear and remaining tyre life using your own measured wear rate.
Magnetic pull measurements
Record repeated pull readings, inspect their mean and range and compare static magnetic load with optional class limits.
Measured clearance curves
Interpolate between measured magnetic-pull and clearance points, and explore the effect of tyre wear within that measured range.
Test one change at a time
Visual ballast planning
Click or drag ballast positions on a schematic, try target rear loads and keep the plan separate from a measured baseline.
A-B-A comparisons
Return to a baseline after a change to inspect drift, using frozen setup snapshots to keep each test’s configuration clear.
Electrical losses
Use loaded DC measurements to explore voltage drop, resistance and power loss through the electrical path.
Motor test records
Record force and lever-arm measurements to calculate torque, power and supported efficiency estimates.
Race strategy calculations
Explore race duration, incidents, pit-stop costs and the laps needed to recover lost time.
Class limits and margins
Compare supported setup measurements with limits and see how much margin remains.
Compound gears and rotating mass
Explore compound ratios, spur-gear geometry and the equivalent inertia of rotating components.
Coast-down and measurement bounds
Analyse measured speed/time traces, distance and deceleration, or inspect how measurement ranges affect supported calculations.
Learn from recorded laps
Type or paste lap times
Bring times from a timer, spreadsheet or notebook in supported seconds or minute-and-second formats, then review the imported laps.
Read results from Paddock
Connect to a Paddock host to read finalised Timing results, including supported corrections and withdrawals, and analyse imported runs offline.
Pace and consistency
Inspect best eligible laps, median pace and interquartile spread, with rolling pace to reveal changes through a run.
Stints and uninterrupted runs
Compare opening and closing pace and best continuous five-lap sequences, with gaps and excluded laps breaking the sequence.
Pit and invalid lap review
Keep excluded laps visible in the record while leaving genuine slow laps in the analysis unless you mark them otherwise.
Compare lap progression
Overlay runs and review pace differences alongside driver, track, lane and condition compatibility.
Progress and local records
Follow median pace, best laps and consistency over time, with the recorded setup changes and eligible local records for context.
Save, compare and share your work
Setup Library
Name, search, sort and annotate saved configurations, then load, rename or save a copy for a new experiment.
Setup comparisons
See absolute and percentage differences between saved setups, with neutral trade-offs rather than treating every increase as an improvement.
Share a setup
Export an individual setup for another user to open, or transfer a setup library through its import/export workflow.
Portable comparison reports
Export a self-contained HTML comparison that another person can open, read and print without your database.
Drafts and separate backups
Keep your working draft automatically and use the separate setup and lap-data backup workflows to protect saved work.
Calculations explained
Read formula examples and assumptions, and keep useful results pinned while collapsing inputs you are not changing.
Livery: Turn a car view into a template
Vector and photograph imports
Prepare SVG, EPS or supported vector PDF artwork, choosing a PDF page, or use PNG, JPEG and WebP photographs for manual tracing.
Six independent car views
Build front, top, left, right, rear and angled views as separate parts of a project, each with its own prepared artwork.
Paintable areas and labels
Select enclosed areas or box-select several, then label bodywork, windows, lights, wheels, tyres, trim, interior and chassis.
Recover small and enclosed areas
Bring back filtered small shapes or enclosed white areas, and trace missing regions by hand before painting.
Protect the reference details
Keep selected artwork as reference only, or use preparation roles to distinguish bodywork, protected details and hidden elements.
Reusable car templates
Save prepared views in your library and return to template preparation when the design needs another paintable area.
Paint a scheme with character
Whole panels or individual areas
Apply a colour to an entire labelled part of the car or work on individual regions for more detailed schemes.
Multi-stop gradients
Blend two to eight colour stops and adjust their positions, direction and strength.
Finish previews
Explore matte, satin and gloss appearances with metallic or pearl options, and toggle the finish preview while checking the artwork.
Paint references and notes
Keep the chosen paint references and workshop notes alongside the visual design.
Shapes and Bézier curves
Create rectangles, ellipses and freeform colour blocks, then refine their anchors and handles.
Lines, pinstripes and racing stripes
Draw open lines with controlled thickness and end caps, or use single, double and triple stripes with adjustable colours, widths and gaps.
Decals, lettering and race numbers
Import your artwork
Place graphics with transparency, including supported SVG, EPS and PDF artwork, then resize and rotate them on the car view.
Bring designs from Decals
Open .sfdecal packs or .sfsheet files, select individual decals or groups and add them to your library or place them on a view.
Separate artwork from a sheet
Select crop regions from an SVG or PDF sheet, remove a plain white background where suitable and reuse the chosen graphics.
Text and race numbers
Create lettering and numbers with your chosen typeface, colour and position.
Custom fonts
Load TTF, OTF, WOFF or WOFF2 fonts for the project without installing them into the operating system.
Fit and organise the design
Perspective fitting
Use skew, compression and pinch presets or fine adjustments to fit artwork to an angled 2D car view.
Layers and editable groups
Reorder layers, select several objects and group them while retaining access to the individual children.
Controlled resizing
Scale groups proportionally with handles, exact fields or percentages, including fitted artwork and stripe gaps.
Copy appearance
Reuse an object’s appearance on other elements to keep the design consistent.
Canvas tools
Pan and zoom, use the grid and snapping, and experiment with Undo/Redo while positioning details.
Reuse, exchange and take it to the workshop
Searchable User Library
Search, sort and rename templates, liveries, images, fonts and artwork in one place.
Reusable artwork groups
Save useful combinations to the library and bring them into another project without rebuilding them.
Try a livery on another car
Reuse a saved design on a different template, then adjust placement to suit the new body shape.
Share editable .sfpaint packages
Export selected library items or a complete project with its template and artwork. Recipients import independent copies.
Workshop PDF
Export car views, paint references and notes as a practical visual guide for preparing the model.
Transparent PNG export
Export a chosen view at 1,000–4,000 pixels with an optional finish preview and transparent background.
Local projects and backups
Keep projects in a local library and export separate backups or selected packages for moving and protecting your designs.
Decals: Prepare the artwork you want
Image and vector imports
Bring PNG, JPEG, WebP, SVG, EPS and PDF artwork, with page selection for multi-page PDFs and supported vector detail retained.
Crop and clean backgrounds
Crop images, remove simple edge-connected backgrounds and trim transparent edges, with the original available to restore.
Flat-colour vector tracing
Trace suitable logos into vectors, compare the result with the original and adjust colour, detail and transparency.
Recolour or remove traced shapes
Refine a trace by changing colours or removing shapes, then keep it as a separate copy or replace the current artwork.
Vector artwork cleanup
Select and remove unwanted paths, such as a white background, while retaining white details you have not selected.
Silhouettes and cut-outs
Build an adjustable outer silhouette with internal cut-outs while keeping the source artwork available.
Create your own racing graphics
Editable text and curved lettering
Set lettering, fonts and spacing, or bend text along an arc for badges and curved designs.
Custom fonts
Use imported fonts in your artwork and retain supported font data when sharing editable sheets and decal packs.
Shapes and number plates
Draw precisely sized shapes, stars, arrows, shields and roundels, including oval or rectangular number plates.
Racing stripes
Build one to twelve stripes with adjustable widths, gaps and alternating colours as an editable group.
Checkerboards
Choose rows, columns and cell dimensions for a checkerboard that stays editable.
Editable paths and curves
Draw freehand or place precise points, then adjust Bézier handles, corners and inserted or deleted points later.
Merge, cut and overlap
Combine supported native filled shapes with union, subtraction, intersection or exclusion, including holes and curves.
Get the printed size right
Exact dimensions in millimetres
Set the printed width and height with linked proportions or independent dimensions.
Convert between model scales
Resize from known original dimensions and scales, applying the change to a selection or complete artwork.
Side and top car previews
Try decals at physical size on a car reference, using actual car dimensions or an uploaded image.
Separate placement from printing
Experiment with positions on the car preview while keeping the print-sheet arrangement separate; size changes remain connected.
Plain-paper sizing proofs
Export a proof with labelled 100 mm and 50 mm bars and print at Actual size / 100% to check the result on the model.
Build a practical decal sheet
Paper sizes and multiple pages
Use A4, A5 or 4 × 6-inch photo paper in portrait or landscape, retaining artwork dimensions across pages.
Selection, groups and layers
Select multiple decals, group or lock elements, control their order and use Undo/Redo while arranging the sheet.
Repeat, align and distribute
Create rows and columns with chosen gaps, line up selected decals and move artwork between pages.
Auto-arrange without resizing
Pack decals inside the chosen margins and add pages as needed while preserving their physical sizes.
Rulers, margins and print checks
Inspect placement, cut gaps, margin problems, low-resolution artwork and white-ink settings before export.
Slice, export and prepare to print
Slice part of a sheet
Select an exact millimetre rectangle, clip the artwork or include whole intersecting decals, and keep the original sheet unchanged.
Save a slice as reusable artwork
Add a selected region to the decal library as a group, retaining supported fonts and white-ink settings.
Print an area or export a crop
Print a selected area in its original paper position or export a cropped PDF without rescaling the artwork.
PDF and SVG output
Export PDFs at the intended physical page dimensions, preserve supported vectors and export individual artwork as SVG.
White-ink separation
Prepare a named white separation with per-decal backing or white-only options for a compatible print workflow. Physical printer validation is still pending.
Share designs and build your library
Decal and sheet libraries
Organise reusable artwork and finished sheets with names, tags, search, sorting and grid or list views.
Independent working copies
Edit artwork on a sheet without changing its saved library master, so a reusable design stays ready for other projects.
Share .sfdecal packs
Bundle reusable decals for another user to import, with supported artwork and font data included.
Share .sfsheet projects
Exchange selected sheets or pages with their paper settings, physical dimensions and artwork for further editing.
Use your artwork in Livery
Import shared Decals packs or sheets into Livery to try individual graphics on a car design before preparing the model.
Keep your work recoverable
Working-sheet autosave
Keep current work automatically and explicitly save sheets to the library when you want to retain them there.
Version history
Preview an earlier saved version and recover it as a separate copy without overwriting the current design.
Complete database backups
Export a .sfdb backup containing saved sheets, artwork, fonts, history and settings for recovery or moving computers.

Paddock.title: Your collection. Your workshop.
Paddock.first: Add your first car, attach a photograph and open Showroom.
Paddock.storage: Your collection lives locally in your user profile, separately from the app. Use complete backups to move it; copying the executable does not copy your collection.

Circuit.title: From an idea to a circuit.
Circuit.first: Choose a track pack, Routed Wood or FreeForm Drawing and start a layout.
Circuit.storage: The desktop app saves on your computer. The online version saves in your browser. Export workspace backups to move or protect your designs.
Circuit.featureNote: Dimensions and clearances are planning aids. Live Preview illustrates motion rather than predicting lap times. Construction exports still need your own CAD/CAM and cutter setup.

Timing.title: Make race day your own.
Timing.first: Add drivers, cars and a track, then choose a race setup. Use a supported simulation option to explore without hardware.
Timing.storage: Keep the app’s saved race data and settings backed up using its documented export and backup workflows. Share individual layouts and sets without exchanging the entire database.
Timing.featureNote: Race Systems are simulations; available combinations depend on the session format. Physical power and light control depend on the connected interface and relays.

Telemetry.title: Understand your next change.
Telemetry.first: Enter the pinion, driven gear and rear tyre diameter. Save a setup, make one change and compare.
Telemetry.storage: Your draft, saved setups and lap libraries are stored on this computer. Setups and lap data have separate backup workflows; follow the guide for both.
Telemetry.featureNote: Telemetry analyses measurements and recorded laps; it does not perform live lap timing. Calculations and handling suggestions depend on the measurements and assumptions you provide.

Livery.title: Give your car its own identity.
Livery.first: Add a car view, import artwork, label its paintable areas and try a base colour.
Livery.storage: Projects and library items are stored locally in SQLite. Export separate backups; larger collections can be shared or backed up in selected packages.
Livery.featureNote: Livery is a 2D design tool. Finish previews and workshop PDFs are visual guides, not calibrated paint matches or automatic 3D wrapping.

Decals.title: From artwork to decal sheet.
Decals.first: Choose a paper size, import artwork, set its printed dimensions and make a plain-paper sizing proof.
Decals.storage: Sheets, artwork, fonts and history are stored separately from the app in your Documents workspace. Use Backup & Recovery for complete backups.

showcase.title: Race night, your rules.
showcase.text: From a few practice laps to a club championship: run your races, shape the strategy and build your own timing screens.

showcase.title: A home for every car.
showcase.text: Bring your collection to life with photographs, track every workshop change, and share selected cars with fellow collectors.

showcase.title: Your next track starts here.
showcase.text: Try a new layout, plan the space and share an editable circuit. Download Circuit or start designing in your browser.

showcase.title: Small details. Your signature.
showcase.text: Arrange artwork at the sizes your model needs, print a decal sheet, and send editable designs to another builder.

showcase.title: Make the grid your own.
showcase.text: Explore colours, stripes and race numbers on editable car templates. Share your project and let a friend create their own version.

showcase.title: Find the story in your laps.
showcase.text: Explore setups, compare recorded runs and share a readable report of what changed on the track.

Timing.title: Your race-day ideas can travel.
Timing.text: Share your race screens, widgets, sounds and artwork with another racer or club.
steps: Choose your creations
In App Settings → Import and Export, select designs and any related items they need.
Export and send
Export individual designs or create a Content Pack, then send the file to another Timing user.
Make it their own
Individual imports add copies. Content Packs can add editable copies to the normal editors.
Timing.note: Use individual exports for sharing designs. A complete backup is for moving or restoring an installation and includes its database and settings.

Paddock.title: A great car deserves to be shared.
Paddock.text: Give another collector a head start with car profiles, photographs and your chosen setups.
steps: Choose the cars
Open Import & Export → Choose cars, or use More → Export this car on a profile.
Send a car file
Export selected public car details and the main photo, with optional extra photos and setup snapshots.
Review and add
The recipient reviews incoming cars and chooses the fields to accept into their own collection.
Paddock.note: Selected-car files leave out private ownership details, private notes and workshop records. Dealership Mode is separate: it shares a full collection between trusted computers on a local network.

Livery.title: Your design. Their next inspiration.
Livery.text: Share templates, liveries or complete projects for another builder to make their own.
steps: Choose what travels
Open Import & Export → Export a package and select the library items or projects to include.
Send the package
Share the .sfpaint file. Projects carry their car template and embedded artwork.
Keep creating
The recipient chooses Import a package. Independent copies are added to their Livery library.
Livery.note: Share artwork and fonts you have permission to redistribute. Packages can include the original embedded files.

Decals.title: Build a collection together.
Decals.text: Trade individual decals or complete sheets that friends can edit for their own models.
steps: Pick a sheet or pack
Export selected sheets or pages from Sheet Library, or choose saved decals in Import & Export.
Send the editable file
Use .sfsheet for sheets with artwork, fonts and sizes, or .sfdecal for a pack of reusable decals.
Import and personalise
The recipient imports the file into Decals and works with their own copies. A PDF is available for printing or viewing.
Decals.note: Sharing works by sending files; no online account is needed. Use artwork and fonts you can redistribute. Decals and Livery each use their own editable package formats.

Circuit.title: Let someone else take the next corner.
Circuit.text: Exchange editable layouts and track pieces, or share a PDF plan for the build.
steps: Choose your design
In Import & Export, select the current track, a saved Track Library entry or a track pack.
Export and send
Export track JSON for a complete editable design, or pack JSON for reusable piece definitions.
Open and keep
The recipient imports the track and saves it to their library. Pack imports add reusable pieces to My packs.
Circuit.note: Track JSON includes its piece definitions. Importing a track offers the chance to export the current drawing before replacing it.

Telemetry.title: Bring the results to the conversation.
Telemetry.text: Share the lap statistics, setup differences and context behind your comparison in a portable report.
steps: Choose the comparison
Open Compare runs or Progress and select the runs you want to discuss.
Export a report
Choose Export comparison report and send the saved HTML file.
Read it anywhere
The recipient opens the report in a browser to read or print it, without needing Telemetry.
Telemetry.note: Reports capture a snapshot of the comparison. Later corrections in Telemetry do not update an already exported report.
